reference.title: AuditX Glossary of Terms
reference.shortdesc: Definitions of key terms and concepts used throughout the AuditX system and documentation.

dlentry.dd: A comprehensive order verification and visual documentation platform designed for eCommerce and logistics operations. Combines barcode scanning, video/image capture, and integration with order management systems.
The web-based administrative portal for AuditX. Administrators use Forge to configure workflows, manage users, access reports, and control system settings.
The hardware component of AuditX that captures video and images at packing stations. Examples include AHD-100 series. Devices connect to barcodes scanners and cameras.
A physical location (warehouse, fulfillment center, distribution center) where AuditX devices are deployed. Each site has its own configuration, users, and event data.
A predefined configuration that governs how AuditX captures, records, and verifies packing operations. Three workflow types: Order Verification, Video Recording, and Image Logging.
Workflow type that validates each scanned item against order specifications from Shopify or other eCommerce platforms. Records video linked to verification data.
Workflow type that captures the complete packing process as continuous video linked to order or barcode IDs.
Workflow type that captures high-resolution still images at scan points during packing, creating a quick verification record with minimal storage requirements.
A single recording session captured by an AuditX device. Events contain video, images, metadata, and are linked to one or more barcode scans.
Individual actions or scans that occur within a main event. Examples: individual SKU scans during a multi-item order packing session. Sub-events can be captured as images or marked in video.
A machine-readable code (typically numeric or alphanumeric) that identifies products, orders, or items. Scanned during packing to trigger event recording and verification.
A named attribute in AuditX that represents the type of barcode being scanned. Examples: SKU, Order ID, Product ID, Item Code.
A rule using regular expressions that groups barcodes into categories based on their format. Useful for distinguishing different barcode types in mixed-SKU operations.
Optional feature that allows operators to control recording using special barcodes. Examples: <<stop>> barcode to end recording, <<capture>> barcode to take snapshot.
Invisible ASCII codes sometimes added by barcode scanners to barcode data. Can cause scanning errors if not suppressed.
Role with full system access. Admins create users, configure workflows, manage sites, and access all reports and system settings.
Sub-admin role with most capabilities of Admin but with restrictions on user creation, device access, and system configuration.
Role with read-only access to dashboards and reports. Supervisors monitor operations but cannot modify configurations.
Role with access to device touchscreen only for performing packing activities. Operators cannot access Forge portal or modify settings.
System of assigning permissions to users based on their role. AuditX implements RBAC to ensure users access only features appropriate for their responsibilities.
The length of a recorded event in minutes. Max event duration can be configured (typically 3 or 5 minutes). Longer recordings are segmented into multiple events.
The quality of recorded video. AuditX supports 4K (Ultra HD) for highest quality and 1080p (Full HD) for standard quality with smaller file size.
Technique for reducing video file size. AuditX offers Standard compression (broader compatibility) and Advanced compression (higher compression ratios).
Metadata displayed on video or images that remains constant (e.g., Event ID, Barcode, Timestamp, System Name). Overlaid on all frames of recording.
Metadata that changes during video playback to show real-time information (e.g., sub-event markers showing individual SKU scans, weight data at specific moments).
The visual size of overlaid metadata on video. Options: Small, Medium, or Large. Larger sizes may obscure more of the video content.
An automated mechanism to send event data from AuditX to external systems (Shopify, WMS, custom APIs). Enables real-time data synchronization.
A preset package combining workflows, webhooks, and settings into one assignable unit. Config Groups can be deployed to multiple devices simultaneously.
Searchable, filterable record of all recorded events. Reports show barcode, event ID, timestamp, video/images, duration, and webhook status.
Feature that generates shareable URLs for each event recording. URLs allow viewing videos/images without logging into AuditX.
Comma-separated values file format for exporting report data. Can be opened in spreadsheet applications for analysis and compliance documentation.
Authentication credential used to connect AuditX with external systems like Shopify or custom applications.
Pattern matching syntax used to define barcode classification rules. Example: ^[0-9]{12}$ matches any 12-digit number.
Precise date and time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) automatically recorded for each event. Used for audit trails and event sequencing.
Billing unit in AuditX representing recording capacity. Video and image events consume credits. Account runs out of credits when balance reaches zero.
Situation where an AuditX account has consumed all available credits. System can either stop recording or overwrite older events based on configuration.
The specific area of the camera's view that will be recorded. Setting ROI excludes irrelevant areas and optimizes storage use.
Leading eCommerce platform. AuditX integrates with Shopify to access order data for verification workflows.
The unique identifier of your Shopify store (e.g., "mystore" from mystore.myshopify.com). Required for Shopify integration setup.
Authentication credential issued by Shopify that allows AuditX to access your store's order data. Generated in Shopify Admin dashboard.
Unique identifier (ID) assigned by Shopify to each customer order. Linked to video/image events in AuditX for complete order tracking.
